parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one file, src/products/presentation/products.controller.ts, which declares one class, ProductsController. That class handles one concern: the HTTP endpoints for products (create, list, get, update, change status, delete). Each handler only reads request parameters and passes them on to the application layer. None of them holds business rules, validation or invariants, so nothing is duplicated. Reads go through QueryBus (GetProductQuery, GetProductsQuery). Writes go to the injected use-case services (CreateProductService, UpdateProductService, ChangeProductStatusService, DeleteProductService). This read/write split is applied the same way everywhere: every read uses the bus and every write uses its service. So it is a deliberate convention, not a bypass of the module's own abstractions. Mixing a bus with direct services is a small style point, not a cohesion failure. Import direction is out of scope.
